article_title: Edelbyte Launches With $70 Million for an AI-Agent Data Platform; Outlets Differ on Whether Its Under-100-ms Latency Is a Claim or an Aim

content_preview.title: Edelbyte Launches With $70 Million for an AI-Agent Data Platform; Outlets Differ on Whether Its Under-100-ms Latency Is a Claim or an Aim
content_preview.summary: Tel Aviv-based Edelbyte launched on November 11 with $70 million; CTech reports a $25 million seed and a $45 million Series A at a $500 million valuation. SiliconANGLE calls its 100 ms latency a claim, Blocks & Files an aim; none of three outlets names a customer.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Edelbyte Ltd., the developer of a data analytics platform optimized for AI agents, launched on November 11, 2026 with $70 million in funding, according to [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/11/edelbyte-reels-in-70m-for-its-multi-purpose-data-analytics-platform/). [CTech](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/rk9dvkfrmx) reports that the money came as a $25 million seed round led by Sequoia Capital, followed by a $45 million Series A led by Quiet Capital, with p...

editor_notes.content_quality: A 751-word News article on a funding announcement, organised as overview, founders, what the company says it built, a table-style list of figures on which the three reports differ, and an explicit list of what none of them reports. Neutral tone, no promotional language, attribution on every product claim, and the article states up front that the platform description rests on the company's own account. Scope: an AI-agent data-analytics and search engine (Kusto/Azure Data Explorer lineage; competes with Snowflake, Databricks, ClickHouse) is data infrastructure for developers and AI builders, inside the newsroom's software-development/AI focus; it is a funding story, so topic Business & Industry / Funding.
editor_notes.source_verification: Snapshots read from disk (sha256 of decompressed content matches manifest for all three; all HTTP 200, suspicious_patterns null for all three). Live re-fetch with a browser User-Agent returned the same pages (same sizes for SiliconANGLE and Blocks & Files; CTech live HTML differs in size from the snapshot, 237349 versus 266580 bytes, but still contains the article sentences checked by grep). source-0 SiliconANGLE (Maria Deutscher, updated 18:19 EST November 11 2026): confirms 'launched today with $70 million', two rounds led by Sequoia and Quiet Capital with Greenoaks and Swish Ventures, 'According to CTech, Edelbyte is valued at $500 million' (valuation is CTech-sourced), Tel Aviv-based, 'former Microsoft Corp. executives', 'helped develop Azure Data Explorer', Snowflake and Databricks, hundreds of petabytes per deployment, query federation, index automation ('According to Edelbyte'), the verbatim Aharoni quote, 'Edelbyte claims that its platform can query multipetabyte datasets with under 100 milliseconds of latency', 'Edelbyte says several Fortune 500 customers use its platform to power petabyte-scale data environments', and funding use. No price, no named customer, no benchmark, no availability date. source-1 CTech (Meir Orbach, 16:00 11.11.26; Calcalist's English site, a separate outlet from the other two): headline 'Former Microsoft engineers raise $70 million' (so CTech does report the $70 million itself), $25 million Seed led by Sequoia Capital and $45 million Series A led by Quiet Capital, Greenoaks and Swish participation, 'The latest financing values Edelbyte at $500 million', founded November 2025, the four named founders and titles, 'approximately 20 years of experience at Microsoft', Ryzhyk and Sloutsky in the original Kusto team, about 40 people, offices in Tel Aviv and San Francisco, Fortune 500 operating claim with sectors (information security, automotive manufacturing, financial services) but no names, Snowflake/Databricks/ClickHouse, $300 billion market estimate, 'returns results in milliseconds and handle thousands of concurrent queries' with no 100 ms figure anywhere on the page (grep). source-2 Blocks & Files (Chris Mellor, Published Fri 13 Nov 2026 15:26 UTC): '$70 million in seed and A-round funding', 'The company says that it aims to make real-time performance, meaning less than 100 ms, practical and cost-efficient at a hundreds of petabytes scale', 'The cost part is $0.01/GB ingested data with full indexes.' (no billing period or attribution, as the article says), 'search, analytical queries, vector, graph, geospatial and more', on-premises/any cloud/self-hosted, unified query engine and federated queries, 'worked on Azure Data Explorer', 'four early customers in the Fortune 500 area and petabyte-level deployments', competitor list ClickHouse, Databricks, IBM, Microsoft, Oracle, Snowflake; no valuation. Every quoted string in the article was found verbatim on the page it is attributed to; bylines and dates in the article match the pages. First-party source: none cited; edelbyte.com serves only a parked redirect page (/lander) so no company release could be read, and the Wayback capture nearest to it is from July 2025, before the announcement. Allowlist: siliconangle.com, calcalistech.com and blocksandfiles.com are all listed; no addition needed. Independence: three distinct outlets, but all describe the product from the company's own statements and only CTech adds reporting on rounds and valuation; SiliconANGLE takes the valuation from CTech. This is described in the article ('rest on the company's own account') and the article does not claim independent confirmation. Anthropic disclosure: not required - no Anthropic or Claude product or company appears anywhere in the article (grep for anthropic and claude returns nothing); the subjects are Edelbyte, Microsoft, Sequoia and the named competitors.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Headline: '$70 Million' is reported by all three outlets (CTech in its headline, SiliconANGLE in body and title, Blocks & Files in body); the $25M + $45M composition is CTech's, and the article's remark that the sum is the Herald's own is correct and conservative. 'AI-Agent Data Platform' is a fair compression: SiliconANGLE 'data analytics platform optimized for artificial intelligence agents', Blocks & Files 'big data analytics for AI agents', CTech 'data platform' for 'the AI era'; the exact phrase is the Herald's. The claim-or-aim clause is accurate: SiliconANGLE says the company 'claims that its platform can query' under 100 ms (a stated capability); Blocks & Files says the company 'aims to make' sub-100 ms performance practical at hundreds of petabytes (a stated goal, at a different scale). Both attribute it to the company and neither reports a test, so this is a difference in how the status of the figure is worded and not a factual dispute; the body says so ('The articles do not reconcile these, and neither does the Herald') and the headline's 'Outlets Differ' is a fair description of the wording difference. Other differences verified on the pages: customers ('several' / 'four early' / sector list), founders ('executives' / 'engineers' / 'worked on Azure Data Explorer'), competitor lists, price (Blocks & Files only), valuation (CTech, repeated by SiliconANGLE with attribution). Absence claims ('none of the three reports an independent test', names a customer, benchmark, general availability) checked by grep against all three snapshots: true. Date: 'launched on November 11' rests on SiliconANGLE's 'launched today' in a November 11 story, consistent with CTech's 11.11.26. One imprecision found in the summary: it says SiliconANGLE calls 'its 100 ms latency' a claim, dropping the qualifier 'under' that the sources and the headline keep; filed as a clarification (subordinate to the headline, which is accurate).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Vendor statements are attributed ('says', 'claims', 'according to the company'), the $0.01/GB figure is presented as unattributed and unexplained, and the article refuses to reconcile the latency wording.
editor_notes.originality: New story. No existing article or open PR on Edelbyte (grep of articles and submissions, gh pr search).
editor_notes.independent_source_count: Three outlets (SiliconANGLE, CTech/Calcalist, Blocks & Files), none first-party. Not an Analysis, so the Analysis independence test does not apply; News needs 3-5 sources and has 3. The company-sourced nature of the product description is disclosed in the article.
concerns: Summary writes 'its 100 ms latency' where SiliconANGLE says 'under 100 milliseconds' and Blocks & Files 'less than 100 ms'; clarification filed.

All product claims (latency, scale, customers, price) are single-account, company-sourced statements relayed by outlets; the article says so and reports no verification, which is the most a funding report of this kind can honestly offer.
recommendations: When a company release or blog is reachable, cite it for the original wording of figures that outlets word differently.
Keep qualifiers such as 'under' in the summary line as well as the headline.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, carefully attributed funding report that is explicit about its limits; every quote and figure traced to the three pages. One summary-level qualifier is dropped, which a clarification covers; no headline, lead or body claim is wrong. Approved with a corrections record. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, accurate funding and positioning report on AI-agent data infrastructure for a defined developer audience, with company-sourced product claims
